title: Hosted Suite PRD: Clarity, Scope Lock, and Launch Checklist for Chat/Completions/Embeddings/Rerank
creator: Asha Patel
description: This PRD defines a scope-locked, testable plan to launch the unified hosted endpoint suite (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) with explicit behavioral contracts, operational readiness gates, and a prioritized launch checklist. The document clarifies functional surface, non-functional constraints, and acceptance criteria targeted to avoid last-minute scope creep ahead of the dedicated launch window.
background: Several previous PRDs covered broad features for hosted endpoints; this ticket consolidates outstanding ambiguities (determinism expectations, kv cache semantics, fallback model mapping, and SDK surface parity) into a single scope-locked deliverable that product, engineering, and design agree is shipment-ready pending the checklist items below.
goals: Ship a consistent hosted API surface for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank that matches documented behavior and SDKs
Ensure operational SLOs are defined and instrumented for 99th percentile latency and error budget per lane
Provide a launch checklist that ties acceptance tests to telemetry and rollback conditions
Minimize customer migration effort by publishing compatibility notes and migration guides
scope_in: API contracts for generation (chat/completions) including structured output and function calling semantics
Embeddings API with stable dimensionality mapping and versioned model names
Rerank API that accepts batched candidates and returns canonical score ordering
SDK method parity for JavaScript and Python (minimal set: create(), stream(), embeddings(), rerank())
Operational dashboards for per-model latency, per-tenant cost, and error rates
scope_out: Multi-modal file uploads (deferred to later cycle)
Full-featured UI components for query builders in Console (design follow-up)
requirements: REQ-01: API surface - single endpoint semantics documented for generation and chat with examples
REQ-02: Determinism - same payload and model pinning must produce stable responses within defined variance for evaluation test sets
REQ-03: KV cache - ephemeral by default with explicit opt-in sticky cache flag for long contexts
REQ-04: Fallback policy - mapping table from high-cost to low-cost models with compatibility labels
REQ-05: Embeddings dimensionality - guarantee shape and normalization used in similarity index docs
REQ-06: Rerank contract - stable tie-breaking rules and score normalization across model variants
REQ-07: SDKs - streaming and non-streaming APIs with consistent error handling and retry semantics
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR-01: Latency - P99 generation latency <= 450ms for small models on hosted tier at baseline traffic profile
NFR-02: Availability - 99.9% uptime for hosted endpoints within scope during business hours
NFR-03: Cost - autoscaling ramp should limit per-token cost degradation to < 25% under 3x baseline traffic spikes
NFR-04: Observability - traces, per-token cost attribution, and per-route histograms must be available in Console
NFR-05: Security - request logging obfuscates PII and adheres to KMS encryption requirements
acceptance_criteria: AC-01: Behavioral tests - a canonical test suite (generation, chat, embeddings, rerank) passes with fixed seeds across models pinned in release notes
AC-02: SDK conformance - JS and Python smoke tests pass and published packages include changelog + compatibility note
AC-03: Telemetry - dashboards show correct per-route latency, cost, and error rates with alerts configured for >2x baseline error rate
AC-04: Rollout gating - canary slice (0.5% traffic) shows no severity >P1 regressions for 48 hours before ramp
AC-05: Documentation - PRDs, API reference, migration guide, and example apps are published and linked in quickstart
AC-06: Security sign-off - InfoSec approves the request/response obfuscation and KMS integration
AC-07: Chaos test pass - simulated node failures show graceful fallbacks and no SLO breaches in defined test harness
launch_checklist: LC-01: Cut API spec (OpenAPI + examples) and publish to docs website
LC-02: Merge SDK release branches and create tagged packages for npm and PyPI
LC-03: Configure canary routing and traffic shaping in control plane
LC-04: Create per-model fallback mapping and pre-warm low-cost variants
LC-05: Validate KV cache opt-in flag and document behavior in API reference
LC-06: Wire Console dashboards and verify data freshness < 90s
LC-07: Run canonical acceptance test suite in staging and attach results to ticket
LC-08: Security and privacy review completed and signed off
LC-09: Runbook updated with rollback steps, owner rotations, and page targets
LC-10: Post-launch monitoring playbook scheduled with SRE and support for first 72 hours
rollout_plan: R1: Internal beta (0% external) - enable feature for Redwood internal orgs and capture feedback for 3 days
R2: Canary (0.5%) - route a 0.5% slice of production traffic, observe for 48h; smoke and behavioral tests run continuously
R3: Incremental ramp - 1% -> 5% -> 20% over multiple days with SRE approval at each gate
R4: Full launch (100%) - after no critical regressions across 7 days of mixed traffic and acceptance metrics stable
monitoring_and_alerts: MA-01: Alert on P99 latency deviation > 2x baseline for generation endpoints
MA-02: Alert on error rate (5xx) > 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes
MA-03: Alert on per-tenant cost anomaly (sudden >3x token rate) to detect runaway usage
MA-04: Synthetic traffic pipeline for canonical prompts to run hourly and post results to a dashboard
MA-05: Rolling log sampling for the first 48 hours of canary to capture edge failures
notes: Decision log: pinned deterministic behavior for eval suites only; production can have controlled variance documented in behavior section
Trade-off: opting for ephemeral KV cache by default reduces cross-tenant leakage risk but may increase repeated token cost for long contexts
Follow-up: Dedicated capacity will expose kernel-config knobs; not in scope for this hosted launch
